title: Staccato eval docket — Tara Wright
body:
Purpose / quick note:
- Fast scratchpad to capture a weird, bursty failure pattern observed during nightly micro-batches (2026-02-28 -> 2026-03-02).
- Keeping raw samples + quick ad-hoc scoring here before formalizing into a replay test.

High-level summary:
- Symptoms: outputs getting truncated mid-sentence then restarting with a short unrelated clause (staccato-like). Usually on longer context (>1,200 tokens) with temperature 0.7. Not isolated to a single model family — seen on rwd-lite-7b and rwd-sustained-13b quantized variants.
- Hypothesis: KV cache eviction race + intermittent kernel fallback causes partial continuation that looks like a new stream chunk. Could be batching edge-case when prefix cache present.

Quick timeline of ops noticed:
- 2026-02-27 23:30 PST: deploy hotfix that changes batching window from 8ms -> 6ms (DEPLOY-1869).
- 2026-02-28 overnight: spike in staccato cases (internal metric: samplestaccato_rate from 0.04% -> 0.67%).
- 2026-03-01: roll back batching window to 8ms; rate drops but not fully to baseline.

Raw example (input + outputs):
- Prompt (trimmed): "Write a friendly explainer about sharding models across GPUs, include tradeoffs and short pseudo code."
- Good output (control):
  "Sharding models across GPUs lets you distribute memory and compute. Common approaches: tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism. Tensor parallelism splits each layer's weights; pipeline stages split consecutive layers. Pseudocode: for shard in shards: load_weights(shard) ..."
- Staccato output (observed):
  "Sharding models across GPUs lets you distribute memory and compute. Common approaches: tensor parallelism, pipeline parallelism. Tensor parallelism splits each layer's weights; pipeline stages split consecutive layers. Pseudocode: for shard in shards: load_weights(shard) ...

Then: 

  'Also, if you need to...

  take the ferry.'

  (weird short clause unrelated to prompt, appears after a short pause)

Manual inspection notes:
- Timestamped token logs show a gap (~120ms) between final token of main paragraph and the stray fragment.
- No HTTP reconnects logged at client layer in the majority of cases.
- Kernel logs show occasional fallback to non-optimized matmul on one host at the exact timestamps.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (quick, non-normative):
- Coherence continuity (0-3): 0 = major interruption & irrelevant fragment; 3 = coherent finalization.
- Start-to-end relevance (0-2): 0 = drift to unrelated content, 2 = stays on topic.
- Restart artifact severity (0-2): 0 = long unrelated fragment, 2 = negligible micro-ellipsis.
- Triage priority = if (Coherence <=1 AND Restart severity <=1) => P0 next 24h; else P2.

Quick scored samples (hand-labeled, N=12):
- 7 samples scored (Coherence:1, Relevance:0, Severity:0) => P0 triage.
- 3 samples scored (Coherence:2, Relevance:1, Severity:1) => P2 watch.
- 2 samples clean.

Immediate reproducibility steps (for SRE / runtime):
1) Re-run failing prompt with exact model + quantization + seq len on host that logged kernel fallback; enable verbose kernel trace (ticket JIRA-INF-4321).
2) Replay same requests with batching disabled on that host for 2 hours to see if rate changes.
3) Collect raw token-stream timeline + kernel logs + process-level scheduling (perf trace).
4) If reproduced, try toggling batching window back to 12ms for a short window and compare.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is there any correlation with CPU steal or noisy neighbor on that host (check k8s metrics)?
- Could prefix/KV serialization mismatch produce a secondary short decode pass? Seems unlikely but need to check cache serialization versioning.
- Client-level: ensure streaming consumer doesn't append buffered fragment when network resumes — but most clients show single TCP session.
- Might be related to recent small change in stream chunk flattening (PR 1893) — ask PR owner to simulate with a probe.

Things to capture for the incident runbook:
- Exact request IDs, host IDs, model binary sha, quantization params, sequence length, batching window value.
- Simple repro harness (python) that calls the same endpoint while toggling small network sleeps in the middle of generation to mimic gap.

Notes for evaluation team (for later formalization):
- Build a small focused playback harness that streams tokens with injected pauses; run through canary fleet.
- Add a synthetic metric in telemetry: "postGen-unrelated-fragment" detection (heuristic: Levenshtein distance between last 40 tokens and the prompt/expected context > threshold).

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Attach sample IDs and raw logs to JIRA-INF-4321 (Tara).
- [ ] Ask runtime team to enable kernel trace for host i-0a12b (Noelle).
- [ ] Create a small unit harness to reproduce with batching window variations (Ethan).
- [ ] Draft a short heads-up note for API beta customers if P0 confirmed (Mika).

Random quick heuristics I scribbled:
- If staccato rate correlates with seq_len distribution tail > 90th percentile -> prioritize KV cache checks.
- If staccato cases tend to be multi-turn > 6 turns -> look at prefix chunking logic.

Slack / logs references:
- slack: #runtime-debug thread "staccato-night-ops" (link pinned in JIRA-INF-4321).
- cpu/mem: k8s metrics snapshot saved in s3://redwood-ops/diag/2026-02-28/staccato-snap-1.json
- gh pr: gh://redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893 (small change in stream flattening)

Final quick thought: this reads like a transient interplay between batching heuristics and kernel fallbacks. If we can't reproduce quickly, add synthetic injected-gap tests into nightly micro-batch harness and revisit after we gather kernel traces.

-- end of scratchpad --

Notes: messy, will clean and move to confluence if we get reproducible sequence.
